$comment: What NickServ is asking for, shared by tests/main/services.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. Both clients offer the login screen at the same moment, so both have to recognise the same sentences — a prompt one device acts on and the other ignores is two clients.
$nicks: Which nicks speak for the network rather than for a person.

nicks.name: somebody whose name merely starts the same way
and one that merely contains it

$prompts: `asks` is whether this is the moment to offer the login screen; `confirms` is whether it says we already got in.

prompts.name: atheme
prompts.text: This nickname is registered. Please choose a different nickname, or identify via /msg NickServ IDENTIFY <password>.

prompts.name: anope
prompts.text: This nick is registered. Please choose a different nick or identify via /msg NickServ IDENTIFY <password>

prompts.name: phrased as an instruction
prompts.text: You must identify to services with your password before you can use this nick.

prompts.name: phrased as ownership
prompts.text: This nickname is owned by someone else. Please choose another.

prompts.name: an answer is not a prompt
prompts.text: You are now identified for kara.

prompts.name: anope's wording for the same
prompts.text: Password accepted - you are now recognized.

prompts.name: logged in
prompts.text: You are now logged in as kara.

prompts.$comment: About a channel, not about you — offering a login here would be nonsense
prompts.name: ChanServ talking about a channel

$secrets: What a line said to services is kept and shown as. `target` is who it was sent to; `shown` is what both clients keep in place of `text`. Only a services bot, only the commands that carry a secret, and only with something after the verb to hide.

secrets.name: an identify with the account named
an identify with the password alone
a password change keeps the setting's name
any other setting is not a secret
a verification code is a proof of the password
asking about a nick gives nothing away
a person is not services, whatever the words
